sections.text: Where \(f'>0\), \(f\) rises; where \(f'\) is increasing, \(f\) is concave up. Rising of \(f'\) is about concavity, not about \(f\) rising. The graph of \(f'\) fixes the shape of \(f\) but not its height: any vertical shift has the same derivative. One given value of \(f\) pins the curve down.
sections.notation: sketch a possible graph of f

problem.text: The graph of \(f'\) is the parabola \(y=\frac{x^2}{2}-2\). Find the \(x\)-coordinate of the relative minimum of \(f\) and of the inflection point of \(f\). Give reasons.

steps.cue: The plot is \(f'\); the question is about \(f\).
Extrema of \(f\): where the graph of \(f'\) crosses the axis.
Minimum asked: which crossing goes from below to above?
steps.why: At \(x=2\) the graph of \(f'\) changes from negative to positive: relative minimum.

steps.cue: Inflection of \(f\): where the graph of \(f'\) turns.
steps.why: The slope of the parabola is \(x\).

steps.cue: The vertex of the graph of \(f'\).
steps.why: At \(x=0\) the graph of \(f'\) changes from decreasing to increasing.
